Welcome to Addington Valley Academy
I am proud to be the Principal of Addington Valley Academy. Our school is an inclusive, nurturing and ambitious community, driven by a clear and powerful vision: “redefining what’s possible for every autistic child, through leading practices, partnerships and heart”
We are a Special School in Croydon dedicated to supporting children and young people with autism and learning difficulties. We offer 150 places for children and young people aged 4–18. We serve the Croydon region and support pupils with autism and a wide range of social communication, cognitive, sensory, and social, emotional and behavioural needs. Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to be flexible and personalised, combining high-quality teaching with therapeutic and relational approaches so that every learner can grow academically, socially and emotionally.
Our vision shapes everything we do. Through leading practices, we commit to evidence-informed, innovative approaches that meet the individual needs of our pupils. Through strong partnerships, we work closely with families, professionals and the wider community to ensure consistent, joined-up support. Above all, we lead with heart, placing care, understanding and dignity at the centre of school life.
Safeguarding is fundamental to this commitment. The safety, wellbeing and voice of every child and young person are our highest priorities. We have robust safeguarding systems, clear procedures and a strong culture of vigilance, ensuring that pupils feel safe, protected and respected at all times.
At Addington Valley Academy, we believe that when children are safe, understood and believed in, they can achieve more than anyone thought possible. I look forward to working in partnership with our pupils, families and community as we build a school where every autistic child can truly thrive.
Anna Huzzey – Interim Principal
Working closely with students’ families is a crucial part of our work at Addington Valley Academy. We want to ensure that the school is doing everything it can to support and nurture students.

Early Years Foundation Stage
Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
At Addington Valley Academy, we recognise that Early Years is at the heart of the school. We use the Characteristics of Effective Learning to support children in becoming motivated, curious, and independent learners. Our practise is built on the understanding that every child learns in their own way and at their own pace, but this can be further supported through the development of enabling environments and have warm, trusting relationships with their class team.
We utilise a broad variety of specialist approaches, such as Attention Autism, a total communication approach and TEACCH within our universal offer, to ensure that we are providing students with the skills they need to develop the foundations for life-long learning and achieving their best outcomes. However, as mentioned, we recognise that each child’s needs are unique and there are times when we require the use of more individualised and intensive approaches. We also offer The Curiosity Approach and Intensive Interaction to ensure we are working at the child’s level and focusing on the development of those foundational skills for learning.
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Guidance (2025) and we use the Differentiated Early Years Outcomes (DEYO), an adapted version of the Birth To 5 Matters document which includes targets from the Autism Education Trust Progression Framework, to help us assess and plan learning that is suitable and appropriate for our students. Whilst we still work towards Early Learning Goals at the end of Reception, we also focus on meeting the ‘End of EYFS’ targets that are written within the child’s EHCP. We ensure students have access to a broad range of the curriculum, where and when appropriate. We focus on securing skills within the Prime Areas of Learning before moving on to more complex and Specific Areas of Learning. Please see below for more information on what this looks like –
From the Summer term, we will begin preparing students for their transition to Key Stage 1. This is taken on an individualised basis and will be focused on the Pathway which the student will be accessing the following year. More information on what this looks like will be communicated to parents by the class teacher.

pageCache.text:
Reading
At Addington Valley Academy we recognise that reading is an essential life skill and we believe that every child is a reader. With this in mind, we have the aspiration that all of our pupils will leave us with functional reading ability, regardless of their needs or abilities. We know that reading is a form of communication and, at its most basic level, it is the ability to recognise and understand vital signs and symbols in the environment in which we live. This Receptive language ability is imperative for our students.
We focus on developing a reading for pleasure pedagogy, engaging learners in reading through the use of a number of specialist approaches such as sensory stories, story massage, colourful semantics and reading based attention autism sessions.
Given the severe and complex learning needs of our pupils and the barriers they face on a day-to-day basis, we appreciate that ‘reading’ may look different for each student. As such, we have developed three reading pathways;
Click here to read our Reading Policy
PHONOLOGICAL READING PATHWAY
THE DEVELOPMENT OF RECOGNISABLE EARLY READING SKILLS FOR DECODING AND COMPREHENSION, THROUGH A SPECIALIST SYSTEMATIC, SYNTHETIC PHONICS APPROACH
SIGHT READING PATHWAY
THE DEVELOPMENT OF RECOGNISABLE EARLY READING SKILLS FOR DECODING AND COMPREHENSION, THROUGH A SIGHT-READING APPROACH.
FUNCTIONAL READING PATHWAY
THE DEVELOPMENT OF RECOGNISABLE EARLY READING SKILLS FOR FUNCTIONAL PURPOSES, THROUGH PECS OR AAC DEVICES.

RSE
RSE provision at AVA is personalised as appropriate to meet individual needs of our students and based on their Age, Physical, mental and emotional development, Religious and cultural backgrounds and Special educational needs and disabilities.
At AVA, we recognise that our pupils need to know how to be safe and healthy, and how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way, enabling them to live meaningful, healthy, safe, lives with independence, happiness and success. We recognise that the level of need and vulnerability of our students alongside a very wide range of barriers to learning mean that teaching these aspects of life in a meaningful way is complex but vital to achieve the greatest levels of understanding and independence possible.

pageCache.text:
Equality & Diversity
Addington Valley Academy is committed to creating an inclusive environment, where people are treated with dignity and respect and where we anticipate and respond positively to different needs and circumstances so that everyone can achieve their potential.
We are committed to promoting and advancing equality of opportunity, not only because it is an important part of the mission, vision and values of the Academy, but also because by attracting and retaining the most diverse range of students, staff and partners, we will ensure the Academy’s future success.
We believe that everyone has the right to be treated fairly and without discrimination, regardless of their circumstances or background and to be appreciated for their genuine self. In particular we make sure that all our policies and practice prevent discrimination against someone on the grounds of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.
We will consult and involve the school community in our decision making.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Addington Valley Academy, Co-educational Special School for children and young people aged 2-19 who have autism and social communication
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Vision
To redefine what’s possible for every Autistic child through leading practices, partnerships and heart.
Our practices reflect our collective drive to ensure every autistic child achieves meaningful success, without limits on their future aspirations. To be a school where special truly happens. We are committed to building a leading curriculum that offers rich opportunities, purposeful experiences, and the highest expectations for all. This will be achieved through effective training and ongoing support in evidence-based autism practices, including TEACCH, Attention Autism, and a Total Communication approach, ensuring staff have the expertise needed to deliver exceptional provision. By maintaining the highest standards of teaching, learning, and achievement, we will continue to provide an inclusive and individualised curriculum that enables every autistic child to thrive and succeed.
At our school, we recognise that transforming lives means going the extra mile in all that we do, building strong and purposeful partnerships at every level. Partnerships begin within each classroom, where every child is truly known and understood, with targets clearly articulated and progress carefully monitored. To ensure consistency and collaboration, every class is supported through our pathway system and a dedicated middle leader, who works closely with staff and in turn is supported by the senior leadership team. Beyond the school, we work closely with other OHCAT schools to ensure the highest quality of provision in key areas such as careers, literacy, and maths. Our partnerships with families are central to everything we do, underpinned by a clear family strategy detailing the universal, targeted, and specific support available. Within the local community and beyond, we actively support colleagues and advocate for our children, establishing ourselves as a recognised provider of leading practices in the field.
Our school culture is built on the belief that every student, family and member of staff is known, valued and respected as an individual, creating a positive, kind and inspirational environment for all. We hold high aspirations for our pupils, supported through detailed pupil profiles and personalised learning plans that reflect who they are and what they need to thrive. We plan for strong attendance in school because our students and families know us, trust us and feel safe in our community. Staff turnover remains remarkably low, reflecting the commitment and shared sense of purpose that binds us together. As a school, we aim to be difference makers; placing the emotional, social and physical well-being of all at the centre of our work. Alongside our bespoke curriculum, we provide a wide range of supportive therapeutic interventions including speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, canine assisted learning, drama and music therapy, rebound therapy and the AVA farm, ensuring every child receives the holistic support they deserve
Values
Wellbeing. Independance. Communication. Achievement.
Our provision and curriculum are grounded in a communication-led, positive-behaviour model. This approach incorporates therapeutic practices, sensory integration, and tailored support that enable students to access both the core and wider curriculum, helping them make sense of the world around them.
Wellbeing – We prioritise the physical and emotional wellbeing of our students and their families.
Independence – We equip students with the skills and confidence they need to prepare for adulthood and thrive beyond their time at Addington Valley Academy.
Communication – We ensure every student can express their wants, needs, and views, empowering them to advocate for themselves.
When students are supported to reach their full potential in Wellbeing, Independence, and Communication, they are able to accomplish meaningful and lasting Achievement.
